meta.title: Jack in the Box — Central Los Angeles NNN parcel
meta.subtitle: Sell-before-expiry vs renew decision workspace (anonymous)
meta.privacyRule: No owner name, entity, street address, parcel number, lease document or owner financial record is published anywhere on this site. Those records stay with authorised advisers in an access-controlled internal workspace. Everything published here is aggregate and non-identifying, and identifiers are replaced with placeholders.
meta.verificationRule: A value is published only when it was read on an official source page during the verification sweep recorded on the Verification page. If a value could not be confirmed, the cell is left blank and the item appears on the Flagged for Review page with a link for manual checking. No value is inferred, estimated or carried over from memory.
meta.decisionRule: No winner between sell and renew is selected. The evidence is not sufficient to price either branch, so the deliverable is a decision gate sequence plus the arithmetic that turns verified inputs into one comparable number.

gates.title: Lease and title facts
gates.question: What exactly does the lease say about expiry, options, notice, rent, escalations and assignment?
gates.criteria: Executed lease and amendments abstracted; estoppel certificate obtained from the tenant; title preliminary report and exceptions reviewed; notice calendar reconciled against the abstract.
gates.evidence: None in the public record. The expiry window 2030–2035 is the owner's brief and is unverified.

gates.title: Tenant credit and renewal intent
gates.question: Will the tenant renew, at what rent, and can it perform through the term?
gates.criteria: Written renewal indication from the tenant; franchisee-level financials for the operating entity; review of the securitisation covenants that constrain closure and rent decisions.
gates.evidence: Verified: FY2025 net loss, 86 closures, franchise rental revenue down 6.8% over the first 40 weeks of FY2026, US$500 million refinancing at 7.624%, CFO transition. None of this is parcel-specific.

gates.title: Trade-area evidence
gates.question: What do the three-mile and ten-minute drive-time rings around this parcel actually show?
gates.blocking: Parcel APN inside the secure workspace
gates.criteria: Census tracts selected and documented; ACS five-year estimates pulled for each indicator; traffic counts from the city or state; competitor and school inventory mapped.
gates.evidence: County and metro aggregates only. These are context, not trade-area figures.

gates.title: Hazard and insurance screening
gates.question: Which hazard zones is this parcel in, and what does cover cost?
gates.blocking: Parcel address inside the secure workspace
gates.criteria: CGS zone result, FEMA flood zone and base flood elevation, fire hazard severity zone, engineering opinion, insurance quotes with deductibles and exclusions, loss-of-rent cover.
gates.evidence: Regional probabilities verified; parcel statuses unknown.

gates.title: Valuation evidence
gates.question: What would a buyer actually pay for this lease today, and what is the short-lease discount?
gates.criteria: At least three written broker opinions of value with short-lease comparables; verified cap rates; reconciliation of the discount against actual quotes rather than a modelled assumption.
gates.evidence: No transaction evidence in the public record. Treasury yield verified as a reference only.

gates.title: Tax and ownership position
gates.question: What is the after-tax number for selling, on this owner's facts?
gates.blocking: Owner records held by the accountant
gates.criteria: Adjusted basis, depreciation history, holding entity, state residency, net investment income exposure, transfer-tax computation, and any exchange capacity confirmed by the accountant.
gates.evidence: Federal and state rate rules verified; the owner-specific inputs are private by design.

gates.title: Decision memo and stress test
gates.question: Which branch survives the base case, the downside case and a black swan?
gates.criteria: After-tax sell proceeds compared with hold net present value under base, downside and black swan assumptions, with observations and assumptions labelled separately and a documented decision date.
gates.evidence: Not started, because the inputs are missing. The calculator exists to run this the day the inputs arrive.

risks.risk: Selling into a market that prices the remaining term as a wasting asset. With a 2030–2035 expiry and a tenant that is closing units, buyers may capitalise a re-leasing cost the owner cannot yet quantify.
risks.evidence: Tenant closures and negative same-store sales (T-01 to T-06); no comparable sale evidence yet (G5).
risks.mitigation: Obtain three written broker opinions with short-lease comparables before setting a reserve price; test the price with and without a renewal commitment.

risks.risk: Tax leakage larger than expected. Depreciation recapture, state tax on the gain and city or county transfer taxes can each move the net number materially.
risks.evidence: Federal recapture maximum 25% (C-03), California top marginal rate 12.3% (C-05); transfer tax rates unverified (F-09, F-10).
risks.mitigation: Have the accountant produce the after-tax number from actual basis and depreciation records; run the calculator only as a sensitivity check.

risks.risk: Loss of optionality if the corridor improves. A sale is irreversible; the surrounding district may densify or gain transit access after closing.
risks.evidence: County population is falling while metro payroll is rising (E-01, E-07), so local direction is genuinely ambiguous.
risks.mitigation: Price the option value explicitly: compare sale proceeds with the hold value under an upside case, not only the base case.

risks.risk: Vacancy at expiry with a specialised building. A drive-through box is costly to re-tenant and may need demolition or conversion.
risks.evidence: No parcel-level market evidence yet; tenant's own closure programme shows the brand will walk away from underperforming sites (T-04).
risks.mitigation: Commission a re-leasing study with conversion cost estimates; confirm zoning allows alternative uses; hold a reserve equal to estimated downtime plus tenant improvements.

risks.risk: Rent interruption and repair cost arriving together after an earthquake or fire, exactly when insurance is expensive or restricted.
risks.evidence: 60% probability of a magnitude 6.7 or greater event in 30 years (H-01); 11,160 housing units lost in the January 2025 fires (E-03).
risks.mitigation: Confirm loss-of-rent cover, deductibles and exclusions; obtain a seismic assessment; keep a liquidity buffer sized to the deductible plus downtime.

risks.risk: Interest-rate drift. A higher exit cap rate at sale reduces terminal value more than the rent collected in the interim adds.
risks.mitigation: Run the hold value at exit cap rates two percentage points above and below the base case; do not rely on cap-rate compression.

risks.risk: Signing a below-market rent for another long term and locking in the loss. Renewal negotiation happens against a tenant with leverage from its own closure programme.
risks.evidence: Franchise rental revenue down 6.8% year over year (T-08); tenant guidance for a further same-store sales decline (T-10).
risks.mitigation: Set a walk-away rent from the hold-versus-re-tenant analysis; require a rent floor, escalation and a termination payment; never negotiate before the lease abstract and the notice calendar are reconciled.

risks.risk: Tenant credit deterioration over a new term, including restructuring or lease rejection in a bankruptcy.
risks.evidence: FY2025 net loss of US$80.7 million and a US$209.6 million goodwill impairment in the same release; US$500 million refinancing at 7.624% (T-11); dividend discontinued (T-10).
risks.mitigation: Request franchisee-level financials and guarantor information; consider a larger security deposit or letter of credit; model a rejection scenario.

risks.risk: Deciding on stale or conflicting demographic figures. Two official agencies currently publish county population estimates that differ by more than 140,000 persons.
risks.evidence: State estimate about 9.8 million for January 2026 (E-01) against Census 9,694,934 for July 2025 (E-04).
risks.mitigation: Use one agency consistently, state which one, and test the direction rather than the level; prefer tract-level ACS for the trade area.

risks.risk: Privacy breach. Publishing or circulating parcel identifiers, lease files or owner finances creates a direct financial and legal exposure.
risks.evidence: Owner instruction on record; no identifier appears in this workspace.
risks.mitigation: Keep identifiers in the access-controlled internal workspace; publish aggregates only; run the identifier scan before every deploy.

risks.risk: Acting on a projection that looks precise but is not supported. A versioned cash-flow model is only defensible once verified inputs and enough comparable history exist.
risks.evidence: No comparable sale evidence (G5) and no owner tax inputs (G6).
risks.mitigation: Label observations and assumptions separately; do not publish a point forecast; back-test any model before relying on it.

risks.risk: Notice deadlines missed while analysis continues, foreclosing an option by default.
risks.evidence: Notice periods, option windows and renewal mechanics are unknown until the lease is abstracted (G1).
risks.mitigation: Abstract the lease first and build a dated notice calendar with named owners and reminder dates before any other work.

blackswans.evidence: 60% probability of magnitude 6.7 or greater within 30 years; 31% for magnitude 7.5 (H-01).
blackswans.channel: Simultaneous rent interruption, structural repair, tenant failure and exit-liquidity loss.
blackswans.preparation: Seismic assessment, loss-of-rent cover, deductible funding, and a written rule that the property is not sold into the first 90 days after an event.

blackswans.evidence: 11,160 housing units lost in January 2025 (E-03); state fire hazard mapping is being updated with a comment window closing 8 January 2027 (H-04).
blackswans.channel: Premium spikes, non-renewal, higher deductibles, and valuation discounts for uninsurable risk.
blackswans.preparation: Test a scenario with no comparable private cover and a FAIR Plan fallback; keep the deductible liquid.

blackswans.evidence: FY2025 net loss, 86 closures, securitisation leverage and leadership turnover (T-04, T-11, T-12).
blackswans.channel: Rent stops, the lease becomes an unsecured claim, and re-leasing starts from zero.
blackswans.preparation: Model a 12 to 24 month vacancy with tenant-improvement cost; prefer security enhancements at renewal.

blackswans.evidence: 10-year Treasury 4.91%; the tenant itself priced secured debt at 7.624% in June 2026 (C-01, T-11).
blackswans.channel: Capitalisation rates widen, buyers thin out, and the sale price falls even though rent is unchanged.
blackswans.preparation: Set a price floor rather than a target; keep the sale decision independent of a rate forecast.

blackswans.evidence: City and county transfer-tax pages could not be verified in this sweep (F-09, F-10).
blackswans.channel: A material, one-off reduction in net sale proceeds, or a cap on rent growth.
blackswans.preparation: Re-verify the current rates at the time of any transaction and model a two percentage point increase in transaction cost.

blackswans.evidence: State population fell 0.14% in 2025 with legal international immigration down by about half and net domestic out-migration of 288,600 (E-02).
blackswans.channel: Lower trade-area demand and higher wage pressure at the same time.
blackswans.preparation: Track quarterly payroll and population releases; treat a second consecutive year of decline as a trigger to re-underwrite.

questions.question: What is the exact expiry date, and do any renewal or extension options exist?
questions.why: Every value calculation depends on the remaining term and on who controls the extension.
questions.document: Executed lease, all amendments, side letters
questions.ifYes: Options shift leverage to the tenant and change the short-lease discount.
questions.ifNo: The owner controls timing and can market a longer lease.

questions.question: What notice periods and deadlines apply to renewal, termination and rent adjustment?
questions.why: A missed notice can remove an option by default.
questions.document: Lease abstract with a dated calendar
questions.ifYes: Build reminders now and work backwards from each date.
questions.ifNo: Confirm in writing that no notice is outstanding.

questions.question: What is the current base rent, the escalation formula, and are there percentage-rent or reporting obligations?
questions.why: Rent and escalations drive both the hold value and the buyer's yield.
questions.owner: Owner's records and the tenant's rent statements
questions.document: Rent roll, escalation schedule, percentage-rent reports
questions.ifYes: Percentage rent adds an upside path tied to sales.
questions.ifNo: Value rests entirely on the fixed rent stream.

questions.question: Is the lease genuinely triple net, and what did the owner actually pay in the last three years?
questions.why: The brief describes a net lease, but the cost-sharing terms decide the real net income.
questions.document: Three years of operating statements and reconciliations
questions.ifYes: Net income is close to base rent, which simplifies the comparison.
questions.ifNo: Capital and operating costs must be modelled explicitly.

questions.question: What assignment, change-of-control and tenant-guarantee provisions exist?
questions.why: They determine what a buyer can enforce after closing.
questions.document: Lease and guarantor financials
questions.ifYes: A guarantee supports value in a sale.
questions.ifNo: Buyers will price the operating entity's own credit.

questions.question: What title exceptions, easements, deed restrictions or recorded conditions affect use?
questions.why: A drive-through use can depend on a recorded condition that a buyer will inspect.
questions.document: Preliminary title report, ALTA survey
questions.ifYes: Any restriction on use or redevelopment must be priced.
questions.ifNo: Redevelopment optionality improves.

questions.question: Has the tenant given any written indication of renewal intent or asked for rent relief?
questions.why: This is the single largest unknown in the renewal branch.
questions.document: Correspondence, estoppel certificate
questions.ifYes: Negotiate terms against a documented position.
questions.ifNo: Model the vacancy case as the base case, not the downside.

questions.question: What are the financials of the franchise entity that operates this restaurant, separate from the brand?
questions.why: The landlord's rent comes from the operator, not from the parent's systemwide sales.
questions.owner: Tenant, through the owner's broker or counsel
questions.document: Franchisee financial statements, guarantor information
questions.ifYes: A strong operator supports renewal and sale value.
questions.ifNo: Assume brand-level credit only.

questions.question: How do this restaurant's sales compare with the system average, and is it on any closure list?
questions.why: A unit below the system average is a candidate for the next closure round.
questions.document: Site-level sales and traffic disclosure
questions.ifYes: Closure risk rises sharply and holding becomes speculative.
questions.ifNo: The unit is a keeper and renewal talks are realistic.

questions.question: Which census tracts fall in the three-mile and ten-minute drive-time rings?
questions.why: W-01 requires trade-area figures, not city or county proxies.
questions.document: APN plus a documented tract list and selection rule
questions.ifYes: Pull ACS five-year tables for each tract and weight them.
questions.ifNo: No trade-area figure can be published.

questions.question: What are tract-level population, households, income, tenure and daytime employment?
questions.why: These drive morning and lunch demand at a drive-through.
questions.document: ACS five-year tables, LEHD workplace data
questions.ifYes: Compare the ring with the county benchmark on E-01 and E-05.
questions.ifNo: County aggregates are only context.

questions.question: What is the five-year tract-level trend, not just the latest year?
questions.why: The brief asks for trend evidence alongside regional figures.
questions.document: Two ACS five-year vintages, matched for comparability
questions.ifYes: Direction confirms or contradicts the county decline.
questions.ifNo: Treat a single vintage as a snapshot only.

questions.question: What traffic counts pass the site, and what are the peak-hour volumes?
questions.why: Drive-through volume is strongly tied to passing traffic.
questions.document: Published count station data, or a purchased count
questions.ifYes: Quantify the site's access advantage.
questions.ifNo: Value the location on rent alone.

questions.question: Which competing limited-service restaurants are within the rings, and what has opened or closed in the last three years?
questions.why: Competitive supply decides whether the unit can grow sales after renewal.
questions.owner: Analyst field survey and business licences
questions.document: Competitor inventory with dates
questions.ifYes: A saturated ring argues for sale or for a lower renewal rent.
questions.ifNo: A thin ring supports renewal.

questions.question: What do the assigned schools and nearby school performance data show?
questions.why: Schools influence household formation and long-run demand in the ring.
questions.document: School assignment lookup and performance data
questions.ifYes: Stable or improving schools support household retention.
questions.ifNo: Plan on flat or declining household demand.

questions.question: Is the parcel in a mapped earthquake hazard zone, and what does the geotechnical report say?
questions.why: Ground failure is a repair and business-interruption risk that insurance may exclude.
questions.owner: Consulting engineer, inside the secure workspace
questions.document: CGS zone result, geotechnical report, seismic assessment
questions.ifYes: Budget mitigation and confirm cover.
questions.ifNo: Shaking risk remains, but ground-failure risk is reduced.

questions.question: What is the flood zone and base flood elevation, and is flood cover required?
questions.why: Flood terms affect financing and insurability.
questions.document: FEMA map determination, elevation certificate
questions.ifYes: Add flood premium and mitigation to the hold case.
questions.ifNo: Confirm in writing with the lender's requirements.

questions.question: What is the fire hazard severity zone classification for the parcel?
questions.why: Classification drives disclosure, mitigation duties and insurance pricing.
questions.document: State fire marshal lookup and local determination
questions.ifYes: Budget defensible-space and hardening costs where applicable.
questions.ifNo: Record the determination with its date.

questions.question: What would insurance cost, what is excluded, and what happens at renewal?
questions.why: An uninsurable asset is a different asset.
questions.document: Two quotes plus a FAIR Plan comparison
questions.ifYes: Feed the premium and deductible into the hold case.
questions.ifNo: Treat insurance availability itself as a risk to be priced.

questions.question: What are three written broker opinions of value for this lease today?
questions.why: W-02 and the short-lease discount require real quotes, not modelled assumptions.
questions.document: Three signed opinions with comparable sales
questions.ifYes: Reconcile the range and use the middle as the base case.
questions.ifNo: No sale price can be defended.

questions.question: What is the observed price difference between long-lease and short-lease net-lease sales in this market?
questions.why: This is the discount the owner is trying to price.
questions.document: Comparable sale set with remaining term and cap rate for each
questions.ifYes: Apply the observed discount instead of a guess.
questions.ifNo: Present a range and label it an assumption.

questions.question: What is the cost to re-tenant or convert the building if the tenant leaves?
questions.why: This sets the floor under the hold decision.
questions.document: Re-leasing study with construction estimates
questions.ifYes: Compare with the sale price net of tax.
questions.ifNo: The vacancy case cannot be sized.

questions.question: What is the adjusted basis and accumulated depreciation?
questions.why: They determine the recapture and the gain.
questions.document: Depreciation schedules and closing statement
questions.ifYes: Compute the after-tax sale number.
questions.ifNo: Only a pre-tax comparison is possible.

questions.question: What entity holds title, and what are the owner's residency and net investment income positions?
questions.why: Entity and residency change both the federal and state result.
questions.document: Entity documents, prior returns
questions.ifYes: Model the actual marginal rates rather than defaults.
questions.ifNo: Use the statutory maximum as a conservative bound.

questions.question: Is there exchange capacity, and what are the deadlines if a sale proceeds?
questions.why: Timing rules can force a decision before the analysis is ready.
questions.document: Exchange plan with dates
questions.ifYes: Sequence the sale with the replacement timeline.
questions.ifNo: The sale is a taxable event and the tax must be paid from proceeds.

questions.question: What are the current city and county transfer taxes on this price?
questions.why: They reduce net proceeds and can be material at higher prices.
questions.document: Escrow estimate
questions.ifYes: Include them in the net number.
questions.ifNo: Do not sign a sale contract without an escrow estimate.

questions.question: What is the decision deadline, and which notices must be served before it?
questions.why: Without a deadline, analysis continues until an option lapses.
questions.document: Decision calendar
questions.ifYes: Work backwards and set interim checkpoints.
questions.ifNo: Set one now, tied to the earliest lease notice date.

questions.question: Who signs off on the final number, and what evidence standard applies?
questions.why: A decision needs one accountable reviewer and one standard.
questions.document: Signed decision memo
questions.ifYes: Publish the memo internally with its assumptions.
questions.ifNo: The decision will not survive scrutiny.

suggestions.title: Reconcile the notice calendar before anything else
suggestions.detail: Abstract the lease, list every notice and option date, and set reminders. This is the only action that prevents an option being lost by default. It requires no judgement about value.

suggestions.title: Request an estoppel certificate and renewal indication together
suggestions.decision: Owner approves the tenant approach and wording
suggestions.detail: A single request for an estoppel certificate plus a written renewal indication resolves the largest unknown in the renewal branch. Timing matters: advisers should confirm that approaching the tenant does not weaken the owner's position.

suggestions.title: Order three broker opinions instead of one appraisal
suggestions.decision: Owner approves the engagement and fee
suggestions.detail: Three independent opinions expose the range and the disagreement. Ask each broker specifically for short-lease comparables with remaining term and cap rate so the discount is observed rather than assumed.

suggestions.title: Build the hazard file with dated determinations
suggestions.decision: Owner authorises parcel lookups in the secure workspace
suggestions.detail: Record the CGS zone result, FEMA flood zone and base flood elevation, and fire hazard severity zone, each with the date of determination. Then obtain two insurance quotes plus a FAIR Plan comparison.

suggestions.title: Select census tracts once and document the rule
suggestions.decision: Analyst confirms the ring definition with the owner
suggestions.detail: Fix the three-mile and ten-minute drive-time rings, list the tracts, and record how they were chosen. Reuse the same list for every indicator so the trend is comparable across years.

suggestions.title: Pull two ACS vintages for the same tracts
suggestions.detail: Compare two five-year vintages on matched geography and check the Census Bureau's comparability guidance first. Publish direction rather than a point forecast.

suggestions.title: Commission a re-leasing and conversion study
suggestions.detail: Estimate downtime, tenant improvement cost and alternative-use feasibility. This sets the floor under the hold decision and defines the walk-away rent in a renewal.

suggestions.title: Run the after-tax comparison only with verified inputs
suggestions.detail: Use the private calculator to produce the net sale proceeds and the hold net present value on the same day, from the same inputs. Keep the output as a dated record, not as a live dashboard number.

suggestions.title: Adopt a three-scenario rule and pre-commit to triggers
suggestions.decision: Owner adopts the rule in writing
suggestions.detail: Define base, downside and black swan cases, and write down in advance what would change the decision, such as a second year of population decline or a failed insurance renewal. Pre-commitment is what stops a drift into the default.

suggestions.title: Keep a decision log with dates and authors
suggestions.detail: Record each input, its source, the date it was verified and who verified it. This site's verification ledger is the template.

suggestions.title: Add a monthly release watch to this dashboard
suggestions.detail: A dated list of scheduled releases (employment, CPI, population, tenant filings) with links. It keeps the evidence current without re-research. Proposed only; not implemented.

suggestions.title: Turn the verification ledger into a machine-checked build
suggestions.detail: The pages on this site are generated from a sourced data file and checked by a script that fails on a missing source, a broken link or an identifier pattern. Extending the same check to every legacy dashboard would stop the older pages drifting out of date.

suggestions.title: Retire the six overlapping dashboards into one
suggestions.decision: Owner chooses whether to keep the archive
suggestions.detail: Parallel sessions produced six dashboards with different cut-off dates. This site is the consolidated entry point; the others are listed under Archive with their cut-off dates so no work is lost and no figure silently conflicts.

suggestions.title: Add a rent-coverage watch at the store level
suggestions.detail: Track the operating entity's sales and occupancy cost against the lease rent once disclosed. Coverage is the earliest observable warning of a closure or a renewal demand for relief.

suggestions.title: Pre-negotiate the sale mechanics before marketing
suggestions.detail: Draft the estoppel, the assignment consent path and the data-room contents before going to market, so a buyer's diligence cannot stall the transaction at the price-discovery stage.

flagged.reason: State estimate about 9.8 million for January 2026 against Census 9,694,934 for July 2025. Different agencies, methods and reference dates; the gap is larger than the annual change.
flagged.verify: Use one series consistently and disclose which; compare tract-level ACS for the trade area.

flagged.reason: The Department of Industrial Relations page states the US$20.00 rate effective 1 April 2024 and did not show a later adjustment during the sweep.
flagged.verify: Re-read the fast food minimum wage page and the Industrial Welfare Commission order before modelling payroll.

flagged.item: Los Angeles city median household income
flagged.reason: The Census QuickFacts page did not load during the sweep.
flagged.verify: Open QuickFacts or the ACS table directly and record the table identifier and vintage.

flagged.item: Los Angeles city minimum wage
flagged.reason: City sites did not load during the sweep; the state minimum wage is verified but a city rate may be higher.
flagged.verify: Check the city minimum wage ordinance page and the current rate letter.

flagged.item: 2026 federal capital gains thresholds
flagged.reason: IRS Topic 409 currently states 2025 thresholds; the 2026 inflation-adjusted amounts were not shown.
flagged.verify: Check the IRS revenue procedure for the 2026 tax year before computing tax for a 2026 or later sale.

flagged.reason: Topic 409 refers to the tax but does not state the rate; the rate page was not retrieved.
flagged.verify: Read IRS Topic 559 and the instructions to Form 8960, then set the rate in the calculator.

flagged.reason: The 2025 rate schedule shows a top marginal rate of 12.3% but not the additional 1% surcharge that applies to very high incomes.
flagged.verify: Confirm with the accountant whether the surcharge applies on the owner's facts.

flagged.item: City of Los Angeles transfer tax thresholds and rates
flagged.reason: The Office of Finance page did not load, so no rate or threshold is published.
flagged.verify: Re-verify on the Office of Finance site and obtain an escrow estimate before marketing.

flagged.item: Los Angeles County documentary transfer tax
flagged.reason: The Registrar-Recorder page did not load.
flagged.verify: Confirm the current county rate with the escrow officer.

flagged.item: Property tax base levy and inflation cap
flagged.reason: The Board of Equalization page did not load; no levy is published.
flagged.verify: Read the county tax bill for this parcel inside the secure workspace.

flagged.item: Parcel earthquake hazard zone
flagged.reason: Publishing a zone determination would identify the parcel. The check must occur in the secure workspace.
flagged.verify: Run the address in the California Geological Survey application and record the result with its date.

flagged.item: Parcel flood zone and base flood elevation
flagged.reason: Same privacy constraint, and the determination needs the exact address.
flagged.verify: Search the Flood Map Service Center and record the map panel, zone and date.

flagged.item: Parcel fire hazard severity zone
flagged.reason: Same privacy constraint. Local responsibility area land is classified by the local jurisdiction, which may differ from the state map.
flagged.verify: Check the state viewer and the local jurisdiction, and record both with dates.

flagged.item: Insurance premium, deductible and exclusions
flagged.reason: Requires the parcel and the owner's loss history; quotes are confidential.
flagged.verify: Obtain two broker quotes plus a FAIR Plan comparison inside the secure workspace.

flagged.item: Building seismic performance and retrofit status
flagged.reason: No public source exists for a specific building's structural condition.
flagged.verify: Commission an engineering assessment and obtain the certificate of occupancy and any retrofit records.

flagged.item: School assignment and performance for the parcel
flagged.reason: Requires the address for assignment, and the state data portal was not retrieved during the sweep.
flagged.verify: Use the district assignment lookup and the state data portal for the identified schools.

flagged.item: Traffic counts at the site
flagged.reason: No public count station is linked to the parcel without the address.
flagged.verify: Request the count from the city or state transportation department, or purchase a count.

flagged.item: Whether the lease is triple net in practice
flagged.reason: The brief describes a net lease; the lease has not been read, so the characterisation is the owner's.
flagged.verify: Abstract the cost-sharing, reimbursement and capital-repair clauses and reconcile against three years of statements.

flagged.item: Short-lease discount percentage
flagged.reason: No comparable sale data exist in the public record for this asset. Any percentage would be an assumption.
flagged.verify: Derive it from the broker opinion comparable set and publish the observed range with each comparable's remaining term.

flagged.item: Anticipated repayment date of the June 2026 notes — two documents in the same filing appear to disagree
flagged.reason: The press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1 on 23 June 2026 says the company has "cleared our near-term maturities, with our next anticipated repayment date in 2029". Item 1.01 of the Form 8-K filed the same day states that the Series 2026-1 Class A-2 notes have an anticipated repayment date of May 2031 and a legal final maturity in May 2056. The 2029 sentence describes the remaining Series 2022-1 notes, not the new notes.
flagged.verify: Read both documents: the release describes the position after the transaction, the 8-K body describes the new notes. The site follows the 8-K body and links both on the sources page.
